synthesis:
Today's screen is a pure US value-and-momentum print: all 10 picks are US-listed, with average Value at the 87th percentile and Momentum at the 84th, while Quality sits at a middling 55. Composite scores compress into a narrow 71.9–85.0 band, so nothing is running away from the pack. Sector distribution is unusually flat — Healthcare is the only cluster at three names (CNC, DVA, BIIB), with seven other sectors taking one slot each. This isn't a thematic screen; it's a cheap-and-moving screen, with yield (75.9 avg) along for the ride.

The Healthcare trio is the cleanest thread: CNC, DVA and BIIB all surface on deep Value plus top-quintile Momentum against a sector median three-month return of -7%, but each carries a Quality flaw the market is already pricing — Centene's -26% ROE, DaVita's 1,261 debt-to-equity, Biogen's pipeline overhang. Separately, CF and APA pair cyclically-cheap multiples (10.1x and 8.5x) with perfect Momentum scores, a commodity-cash-flow trade that reads differently given the macro flag on European energy-grid vulnerability. MO, BBY and ED form the income leg, with dividend yields of 6.09%, 4.93% and 3.29%.

The outlier is ARE — 100th-percentile Value and Yield, but Momentum at 37.5 and ROE of -4.1%, with a flagged dividend cut. The conspicuous absence: zero Technology and zero Financial Services from 149 scored names — a screen this tilted to value mechanically excludes both. Watch the SNAP-cut consumer read against BBY and MO, and any US-Iran energy headline against APA.
